caption: Figure E9-3, the simplified normalized Smith chart two exam questions name parts of. Infinity (the open-circuit point) is at the RIGHT end of the horizontal diameter and zero (the short circuit) at the left - the corrected orientation from the pool's first errata. The horizontal diameter is the chart's only straight line and carries the resistance-circle labels 0, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 20 from left to right; the 1.0 point at mid-chart is the prime center (the normalized system impedance, e.g. 50 ohms). That single straight line is the resistance axis (E9G07). The constant-resistance circles are all tangent at the infinity point and bulge left; the constant-reactance arcs sweep from the rim into the infinity point, labeled 0.2 through 5.0 above the axis (inductive, +jX) with matching magnitudes below (capacitive, -jX), and every arc terminates on the large outer circle - which is the reactance axis (E9G06). As published, there are no wavelength scales around the rim. Redrawn from the NCVEC pool figure.

spoken: A Smith chart titled Figure E9-3: one large circle with a single straight horizontal line through its middle. Infinity is marked at the right end of that line, zero at the left. Along the line, reading left to right, the labels run 0, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 20 - the 1.0 point at the center is the prime center. Circles of constant resistance nest inside the big circle, all tangent at the infinity point and bulging left. Arcs of constant reactance curve from the rim down into the infinity point, labeled 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 5.0 above the line (inductive) and the same below (capacitive). Every arc ends on the big outer circle. The two tested names: the outer circle where the arcs terminate is the reactance axis; the only straight line, the horizontal diameter, is the resistance axis.
